rationale:
T2 is one ε/3 argument, but it rests on four separate obligations with distinct techniques. Each is a genuine standalone lemma, so it is split into four independent children with no sibling dependencies. (1) cbr_rlim_coeffNorm_bound: test forms have bounded Euclidean coefficient norm (finiteness of Simon's |ω|_U of 6.1.15). This is the parent's step 1. (2) cbr_rlim_smooth_cutoff: smooth one-sided cut-off test form η = χω across a level set, the C^∞ version of the γ_ε∘f of Simon Ch. 6, Lemma 4.5(2). These are steps 3-4. (3) cbr_rlim_cutoff_error_le: cut-off error estimate |∫_{f<t} ξ(ω) dμ − ∫ ξ(η) dμ| ≤ M·μ(tsupport ω ∩ {t−ε<f<t}) for an arbitrary admissible (μ, ξ). This covers integrability, linearity and the band bound, i.e. steps 2, 4 and 5, and the parent uses it twice, for (μ_j, ξ_j) and for (μ_X, ξ_X). (4) cbr_rlim_thin_band: continuity-from-above choice of ε > 0 with μ(C ∩ closed band) and ν(C ∩ open band) both < δ. This is step 6 plus the choice at the start of step 7.

The parent proof then reduces to its step 7. Take M from (1) and δ := e/(3(M+1)). Get ε from (4) with C = tsupport ω and ν = μ_X, and χ, η from (2). Apply (3) to (μs j, ξs j) and to (μX, ξX). Apply the limsup hypothesis to the compact closed band K = C ∩ {t−ε ≤ f ≤ t} ⊆ U, which gives eventually μ_j(K) < δ (eventually_lt_of_limsup_lt); the open band is contained in K. Weak convergence at η and the representation identities X_j η = ∫ ξ_j(η) dμ_j, X η = ∫ ξ_X(η) dμ_X finish the argument via the triangle inequality. IsOpen U is not needed.

subproblems.title: Uniform bound on the Euclidean coefficient norm of a test form
subproblems.statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be any set and let ω ∈ 𝒟^k(U) (TestFormOn U k: a C^∞ k-form ω : ℝ^P → Λ^k with compact support and tsupport ω ⊆ U). Then there is a real number M ≥ 0 such that |ω(x)|_E ≤ M for every x ∈ ℝ^P, where |α|_E := covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_{I strictly increasing} α(e_{I(1)}, …, e_{I(k)})²)^{1/2} is the Euclidean coefficient norm of a k-covector α.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (ω : TestFormOn U k), ∃ M : ℝ, 0 ≤ M ∧ ∀ x, covectorEuclideanNorm ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) x) ≤ M
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source (provenance only; the numbered steps below are self-contained): step 1 of the T2 proof (the constant M := sup_x |ω(x)|_E < ∞), i.e. finiteness of Simon's |ω|_U of Ch. 6 (1.15) (book/chapter-06.txt line 178) for a test form. Write w := (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) for the underlying form, so IsTestForm w holds, i.e. w is C^∞ (ContDiff ℝ ∞ w) and HasCompactSupport w, and tsupport w ⊆ U.

1. w is continuous, being C^∞ (ContDiff.continuous).

2. The function n(x) := |w(x)|_E is continuous. By definition |α|_E = sqrt(Σ_{I : Fin k → Fin P} c_I(α)), where c_I(α) := α(e_{I(1)}, …, e_{I(k)})² if I is strictly increasing and c_I(α) := 0 otherwise (e_i = EuclideanSpace.basisFun). For a fixed tuple I, the evaluation α ↦ α(e_{I(1)}, …, e_{I(k)}) is a continuous linear map on covectors (ContinuousAlternatingMap.apply ℝ (Euclid P) ℝ (fun i => e_{I(i)})), so x ↦ w(x)(e_I) is continuous by step 1, and so is its square; the constant 0 is continuous. A finite sum of continuous functions is continuous (continuous_finsetSum) and Real.sqrt is continuous (Continuous.sqrt). (In Lean: unfold covectorEuclideanNorm, then Continuous.sqrt (continuous_finsetSum _ fun I _ => ?_) and split_ifs.)

3. n has compact support. If x ∉ tsupport w then w(x) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport), hence n(x) = |0|_E = 0 (covectorEuclideanNorm_zero). Since tsupport w is compact (HasCompactSupport w), HasCompactSupport.intro gives HasCompactSupport n.

4. A continuous real-valued function with compact support is bounded: by Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support there is M₀ ∈ ℝ with ‖n(x)‖ ≤ M₀ for all x. As n(x) ≤ |n(x)| = ‖n(x)‖ (Real.le_norm_self), n(x) ≤ M₀ for all x.

5. Put M := max M₀ 0. Then 0 ≤ M (le_max_right) and |ω(x)|_E = n(x) ≤ M₀ ≤ M (le_max_left) for every x, which is the claim. ∎
proof_key_steps: The underlying form w of ω is C^∞, hence continuous, and has compact support tsupport w.
x ↦ |w(x)|_E = sqrt(Σ_I [I strictly increasing] w(x)(e_I)²) is continuous: each evaluation α ↦ α(e_I) is a continuous linear map, and finite sums and sqrt preserve continuity.
|w(x)|_E = |0|_E = 0 off tsupport w, so x ↦ |w(x)|_E has compact support.
A continuous compactly supported real function is bounded by some M₀; M := max M₀ 0 is a nonnegative bound.

subproblems.title: Smooth one-sided cut-off of a test form across a level set
subproblems.statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be any set, ω ∈ 𝒟^k(U) (TestFormOn U k), f : ℝ^P → ℝ continuous, t ∈ ℝ and ε > 0. Then there exist a function χ : ℝ^P → ℝ and a test form η ∈ 𝒟^k(U) such that η(x) = χ(x)·ω(x) for every x ∈ ℝ^P, 0 ≤ χ(x) ≤ 1 for every x, χ(x) = 1 whenever f(x) ≤ t − ε, and χ(x) = 0 whenever f(x) ≥ t.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (ω : TestFormOn U k) (f : Euclid P → ℝ) (t ε : ℝ), Continuous f → 0 < ε → ∃ (χ : Euclid P → ℝ) (η : TestFormOn U k), (∀ x, (η : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) x = χ x • (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) x) ∧ (∀ x, 0 ≤ χ x ∧ χ x ≤ 1) ∧ (∀ x, f x ≤ t - ε → χ x = 1) ∧ (∀ x, t ≤ f x → χ x = 0)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source (provenance only; the numbered steps below are self-contained): steps 3-4 of the T2 proof (smooth one-sided cut-off χ and the test form χω). This is the C^∞ replacement of the Lipschitz cut-off γ_ε ∘ f (= 1 on {f ≤ t − ε}, = 0 on {f ≥ t}) in Simon's proof of Ch. 6, Lemma 4.5(2) (book/chapter-06.txt lines 1262-1281); it must be C^∞ because currents act only on smooth test forms. The cut-off is built from the global sets {f < t} (open) and {f ≤ t − ε} (closed), so no compactness argument is needed for it; compact support of χω comes from ω.

1. The set s := {x | f(x) < t} is open (isOpen_lt hf continuous_const) and the set F := {x | f(x) ≤ t − ε} is closed (isClosed_le hf continuous_const). Moreover F ⊆ s: if f(x) ≤ t − ε then f(x) < t because ε > 0.

2. Euclid P is a finite-dimensional real normed space, so Mathlib's smooth Urysohn lemma exists_contDiff_support_eq_eq_one_iff (Mathlib/Geometry/Manifold/PartitionOfUnity.lean), applied with smoothness order n := ⊤ ∈ ℕ∞ to the open set s and the closed set F ⊆ s, gives χ : Euclid P → ℝ with ContDiff ℝ ↑(⊤ : ℕ∞) χ (this is exactly ContDiff ℝ ∞ χ, the order used by IsSmoothForm), range χ ⊆ [0, 1], support χ = s, and (x ∈ F ↔ χ(x) = 1) for all x. (Lean note: in the contract scope `∞` parses as ℝ≥0∞ because of `open scoped ENNReal`; write the order as ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞).)

3. Let w := (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k), so ContDiff ℝ ∞ w, HasCompactSupport w and tsupport w ⊆ U. Define v := χ • w, i.e. v(x) = χ(x) • w(x). Then (a) v is C^∞ of order ∞ (ContDiff.smul applied to χ and w); (b) HasCompactSupport v (HasCompactSupport.smul_left applied to HasCompactSupport w); (c) tsupport v ⊆ tsupport w ⊆ U (tsupport_smul_subset_right χ w). By (a) and (b), IsTestForm v; with (c), v ∈ testFormOnSubmodule U k. Let η := ⟨v, _⟩ : TestFormOn U k; then (η : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k)(x) = χ(x) • w(x) for all x by definition. (Lean note: state (a)-(c) for the function χ • w rather than for a λ-term and build the membership as ⟨⟨(a), (b)⟩, (c)⟩; elaborating HasCompactSupport.smul_left against a λ-term can time out in whnf.)

4. For every x, χ(x) ∈ range χ ⊆ [0, 1], so 0 ≤ χ(x) ≤ 1.

5. If f(x) ≤ t − ε then x ∈ F, so χ(x) = 1 by the equivalence in step 2.

6. If t ≤ f(x) then x ∉ s = support χ, hence χ(x) = 0 (Function.notMem_support).

Steps 3-6 give the four required properties of χ and η. ∎
proof_key_steps: {f < t} is open, {f ≤ t − ε} is closed and contained in it since ε > 0.
exists_contDiff_support_eq_eq_one_iff with n := ⊤ gives a C^∞ χ with values in [0,1], support χ = {f < t} and χ = 1 exactly on {f ≤ t − ε}.
χ • ω is C^∞, has compact support and tsupport (χ • ω) ⊆ tsupport ω ⊆ U, so it is a test form η in U with η(x) = χ(x)ω(x).
0 ≤ χ ≤ 1 from the range; χ = 1 on {f ≤ t − ε}; χ = 0 on {f ≥ t} because such x lie outside support χ.

subproblems.title: Cut-off error estimate for an admissible integral representation
subproblems.statement: Let U ⊆ ℝ^P, let μ be a Borel measure on ℝ^P with μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U, and let ξ : ℝ^P → Λ_k(ℝ^P) (MultiVector P k = continuous linear functionals on k-covectors) be μ-a.e. strongly measurable such that, for μ-a.e. x, |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α|_E for every k-covector α (|·|_E = covectorEuclideanNorm). Let ω, η ∈ 𝒟^k(U), χ, f : ℝ^P → ℝ with f continuous, and t, ε, M ∈ ℝ, such that |ω(x)|_E ≤ M for all x, η(x) = χ(x)·ω(x) for all x, 0 ≤ χ ≤ 1, χ(x) = 1 whenever f(x) ≤ t − ε, and χ(x) = 0 whenever f(x) ≥ t. Then |∫_{f<t} ξ(x)(ω(x)) dμ(x) − ∫ ξ(x)(η(x)) dμ(x)| ≤ M · μ(tsupport ω ∩ {t − ε < f < t}), the measure on the right being finite and read as a real number (ENNReal.toReal).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (ξ : Euclid P → MultiVector P k) (ω η : TestFormOn U k) (χ f : Euclid P → ℝ) (t ε M : ℝ), Continuous f → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → μ K < ∞) → AEStronglyMeasurable ξ μ → (∀ᵐ x ∂μ, ∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) k, |ξ x α| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α) → (∀ x, covectorEuclideanNorm ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) x) ≤ M) → (∀ x, (η : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) x = χ x • (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) x) → (∀ x, 0 ≤ χ x ∧ χ x ≤ 1) → (∀ x, f x ≤ t - ε → χ x = 1) → (∀ x, t ≤ f x → χ x = 0) → |(∫ x in {x | f x < t}, ξ x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) x) ∂μ) - ∫ x, ξ x ((η : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) x) ∂μ| ≤ M * (μ (tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) ∩ {x | t - ε < f x ∧ f x < t})).toReal
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source (provenance only; the numbered steps below are self-contained): steps 2, 4 and 5 of the T2 proof (integrability, linearity of ξ(x) along the cut-off, and the error estimate on the level band), stated once for an arbitrary admissible pair (μ, ξ) so that it applies both to (μ_j, ξ_j) and to (μ_X, ξ_X). The bound uses the open band {t − ε < f < t}; no condition ε > 0 is needed. Notation: w := (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k), v := (η : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k), C := tsupport w, S := {x | f(x) < t}, B := {x | t − ε < f(x) ∧ f(x) < t}, g(x) := ξ(x)(w(x)), h(x) := ξ(x)(v(x)).

1. M ≥ 0, because M ≥ |w(0)|_E ≥ 0 (covectorEuclideanNorm_nonneg).

2. Measurability and finiteness. C is closed (isClosed_tsupport), hence measurable; S and B are measurable because f is continuous, hence measurable (measurableSet_lt). C is compact (HasCompactSupport w, part of ω being a test form) and C ⊆ U (part of ω ∈ TestFormOn U k), so μ(C) < ∞ by hypothesis, and μ(C ∩ B) ≤ μ(C) < ∞.

3. g and h are μ-a.e. strongly measurable. The evaluation map (L, α) ↦ L(α) from MultiVector P k × Covector (Euclid P) k to ℝ is continuous (isBoundedBilinearMap_apply.continuous); ξ is a.e. strongly measurable by hypothesis, and w, v are C^∞, hence continuous, hence a.e. strongly measurable. So g = eval ∘ (ξ, w) and h = eval ∘ (ξ, v) are a.e. strongly measurable (Continuous.comp_aestronglyMeasurable₂).

4. g is integrable. Fix x in the full-measure set where |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α|_E for all α. If x ∈ C, then |g(x)| ≤ |w(x)|_E ≤ M. If x ∉ C, then w(x) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport), so g(x) = ξ(x)(0) = 0. Hence ‖g(x)‖ ≤ 1_C(x)·M for μ-a.e. x. The majorant 1_C·M is integrable, being a constant times the indicator of a measurable set of finite measure (integrable_indicator_iff, integrableOn_const). By step 3 and Integrable.mono', g is integrable.

5. h = χ·g and h is integrable. For every x, h(x) = ξ(x)(χ(x) • w(x)) = χ(x)·ξ(x)(w(x)) = χ(x)·g(x) by linearity of ξ(x) (map_smul, smul_eq_mul). Since 0 ≤ χ(x) ≤ 1, ‖h(x)‖ = |χ(x)|·‖g(x)‖ ≤ ‖g(x)‖ for all x; with step 3, Integrable.mono gives that h is integrable.

6. Rewriting the difference. Since S is measurable, ∫_S g dμ = ∫ 1_S·g dμ (integral_indicator), and 1_S·g is integrable (Integrable.indicator). Hence ∫_S g dμ − ∫ h dμ = ∫ (1_S·g − h) dμ (integral_sub).

7. Pointwise bound: for μ-a.e. x (the full-measure set of step 4), |1_S(x)g(x) − h(x)| ≤ 1_{C∩B}(x)·M. Note that the right side is ≥ 0 by step 1, and write h(x) = χ(x)g(x) by step 5. Cases:
(a) f(x) < t and f(x) ≤ t − ε: then 1_S(x) = 1 and χ(x) = 1, so the left side is |g(x) − g(x)| = 0.
(b) t − ε < f(x) < t and x ∈ C: then x ∈ C ∩ B and the right side is M; the left side is |(1 − χ(x))g(x)| = (1 − χ(x))|g(x)| ≤ |g(x)| ≤ M, using 0 ≤ 1 − χ(x) ≤ 1 and the bound of step 4.
(c) t − ε < f(x) < t and x ∉ C: then g(x) = 0 by step 4, so the left side is 0.
(d) f(x) ≥ t: then 1_S(x) = 0 and χ(x) = 0 (hypothesis), so the left side is |0 − 0| = 0.

8. Conclusion. The majorant 1_{C∩B}·M is integrable (C ∩ B is measurable with μ(C ∩ B) < ∞ by step 2). By step 6, the triangle inequality for integrals (norm_integral_le_of_norm_le) and step 7,
|∫_S g dμ − ∫ h dμ| = |∫ (1_S g − h) dμ| ≤ ∫ 1_{C∩B}·M dμ = μ(C ∩ B).toReal · M (integral_indicator_const, measureReal_def) = M · μ(tsupport ω ∩ {t − ε < f < t}).toReal. ∎
proof_key_steps: M ≥ 0; C := tsupport ω is compact in U, so μ(C) < ∞; C, {f<t} and the band {t−ε<f<t} are measurable.
g := ξ(ω) and h := ξ(η) are a.e. strongly measurable (continuous evaluation composed with (ξ, ω) resp. (ξ, η)).
|g| ≤ M·1_C a.e. (admissibility at α = ω(x), and ω = 0 off C), so g is integrable; h = χg by linearity and |h| ≤ |g|, so h is integrable.
∫_{f<t} g − ∫ h = ∫ (1_{f<t} g − χ g), and the integrand is a.e. bounded by M·1_{C∩{t−ε<f<t}} by a four-case analysis on f(x).
Integrating the majorant gives the bound M·μ(C ∩ {t−ε<f<t}).toReal.

subproblems.title: Choice of a thin level band of small measure
subproblems.statement: Let μ, ν be measures on ℝ^P (Borel σ-algebra), C ⊆ ℝ^P a measurable set with μ(C) < ∞ and ν(C) < ∞, f : ℝ^P → ℝ continuous, t ∈ ℝ with μ{x : f(x) = t} = 0, and δ > 0. Then there is ε > 0 such that μ(C ∩ {t − ε ≤ f ≤ t}) < δ and ν(C ∩ {t − ε < f < t}) < δ (inequalities in [0, ∞], with δ read as ENNReal.ofReal δ).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (μ ν : Measure (Euclid P)) (C : Set (Euclid P)) (f : Euclid P → ℝ) (t δ : ℝ), MeasurableSet C → μ C < ∞ → ν C < ∞ → Continuous f → μ {x | f x = t} = 0 → 0 < δ → ∃ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε ∧ μ (C ∩ {x | t - ε ≤ f x ∧ f x ≤ t}) < ENNReal.ofReal δ ∧ ν (C ∩ {x | t - ε < f x ∧ f x < t}) < ENNReal.ofReal δ
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source (provenance only; the numbered steps below are self-contained): step 6 of the T2 proof (shrinking the band by continuity from above) and the choice of n at the start of its step 7: the closed band B_{1/n} = C ∩ {t − 1/n ≤ f ≤ t} decreases to C ∩ {f = t}, which is μ-null, and the open band B'_{1/n} = C ∩ {t − 1/n < f < t} decreases to ∅. In the application C = tsupport ω, ν = μ_X.

1. For n ∈ ℕ put r_n := 1/(n+1) > 0, A_n := C ∩ {x | t − r_n ≤ f(x) ∧ f(x) ≤ t} and B_n := C ∩ {x | t − r_n < f(x) ∧ f(x) < t}. Since C is measurable and f is continuous, hence measurable, each A_n and B_n is measurable (measurableSet_le, measurableSet_lt, MeasurableSet.inter).

2. Monotonicity. If m ≤ n then r_n ≤ r_m (one_div_le_one_div_of_le), so t − r_m ≤ t − r_n; hence A_n ⊆ A_m and B_n ⊆ B_m, i.e. n ↦ A_n and n ↦ B_n are antitone.

3. ⋂_n A_n ⊆ {f = t}. Let x ∈ A_n for all n. Then f(x) ≤ t (from n = 0). If f(x) < t, choose n with r_n < t − f(x) (exists_nat_one_div_lt, as t − f(x) > 0); then f(x) < t − r_n, contradicting x ∈ A_n. So f(x) = t.

4. ⋂_n B_n = ∅. Let x ∈ B_n for all n. Then f(x) < t (from n = 0); choose n with r_n < t − f(x); then f(x) < t − r_n, contradicting t − r_n < f(x) from x ∈ B_n.

5. Continuity from above. μ(A_0) ≤ μ(C) < ∞ and ν(B_0) ≤ ν(C) < ∞. By tendsto_measure_iInter_atTop (each set measurable, hence null-measurable; the families antitone; one member of finite measure), μ(A_n) → μ(⋂_n A_n) and ν(B_n) → ν(⋂_n B_n) as n → ∞. By step 3 and monotonicity, μ(⋂_n A_n) ≤ μ{f = t} = 0 (measure_mono_null), and by step 4, ν(⋂_n B_n) = ν(∅) = 0. So μ(A_n) → 0 and ν(B_n) → 0 in [0, ∞].

6. Since δ > 0, ENNReal.ofReal δ > 0 (ENNReal.ofReal_pos), so {y | y < ENNReal.ofReal δ} is a neighbourhood of 0 (gt_mem_nhds). By step 5, μ(A_n) < ENNReal.ofReal δ for all large n and ν(B_n) < ENNReal.ofReal δ for all large n; choose N satisfying both (Filter.eventually_atTop applied to the conjunction).

7. Put ε := 1/(N+1) > 0. Then C ∩ {t − ε ≤ f ≤ t} = A_N and C ∩ {t − ε < f < t} = B_N, so μ(C ∩ {t − ε ≤ f ≤ t}) < ENNReal.ofReal δ and ν(C ∩ {t − ε < f < t}) < ENNReal.ofReal δ. ∎
